reading: Each scattered cell lies on one concentric square ring around the grid centre (ring index = Chebyshev distance from the centre); the whole ring is painted that cell's colour, giving nested square rings.

slots.rings: concentric square rings of the grid, index = max(|y-cy|,|x-cx|)
slots.colour_source: the single non-background cell lying on each ring
slots.background: every background cell takes its ring's colour

why: exactly one non-background cell lies on each ring; the output is constant on each ring and equals that cell's colour
invariants: each marker cell keeps its colour

reading: Hollow rectangular outlines fall to the top border and solid crosses fall to the bottom border, each keeping its column and shape and stacking on objects already settled in the same direction (the two groups pass through each other).

slots.subject_up: objects that are hollow rectangular outlines
slots.direction: outlines move straight up, crosses straight down
slots.stop: the grid border or an already-settled object of the same group (stacking, nearest-to-border first)

why: every object keeps shape, colour and columns; outlines end touching the top border or another outline, crosses touching the bottom border or another cross

reading: Every red cell that has no red cell orthogonally adjacent (diagonal contact allowed) turns blue (1); all else unchanged.

new_rows.name: lone4
new_rows.datalog:
orth(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 0.
orth(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DX = 0.
hasnb(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), orth(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, C2).
lone4(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), !hasnb(Y, X).

why: the 4-connected singleton 2-cells are exactly the cells that become 1; no other cell changes

reading: Several 8-framed squares hold a pattern of 2s; all but one share the same 2-pattern. Output is the framed square whose 2-pattern is unique.

new_rows.name: oddbox
new_rows.datalog:
c2(O) :- obj(O, Y, X), cell(Y, X, C), C = 2.
top(O, min(Y)) :- c2(O), obj(O, Y, X).
lft(O, min(X)) :- c2(O), obj(O, Y, X).
rel(O, DY, DX) :- c2(O), obj(O, Y, X), top(O, T), lft(O, L), DY = Y - T, DX = X - L.
differ(O1, O2) :- rel(O1, DY, DX), c2(O2), !rel(O2, DY, DX).
differ(O1, O2) :- rel(O2, DY, DX), c2(O1), !rel(O1, DY, DX).
nsame(O, count(O2)) :- c2(O), c2(O2), !differ(O, O2).
odd2(O) :- nsame(O, N), N = 1.
oddbox(Y2, X2) :- odd2(O), obj(O, Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX.

why: exactly one colour-2 component has a shape no other 2-component has; its box grown by one cell is the 8-framed square that equals the output
invariants: the cut square is copied cell for cell

reading: Four same-coloured (4) cells mark the corners of a rectangle; the cells strictly inside that rectangle are filled with 2.

new_rows.name: inside
new_rows.datalog: inside(Y, X) :- cell(Y1, X1, C), cell(Y1, X2, C), cell(Y2, X1, C), cell(Y2, X2, C), Y1 < Y2, X1 < X2, px(Y, X, B), Y > Y1, Y < Y2, X > X1, X < X2.

why: every cell strictly inside a rectangle whose four corners are marker cells becomes 2; nothing else changes

reading: A 5-separator splits a small legend (a lattice of coloured vertical and horizontal lines, partly covered by a 5 block) from a 4-marker panel; output is the marker panel redrawn: 4s at the panel edges mark line positions, and the k-th vertical/horizontal line takes the legend's k-th vertical/horizontal line colour with the legend's over/under layering at crossings.
verb: redraw legend lines at marked positions

slots.legend: the panel left/right of the full 5 column that holds coloured lines (5 block below)
slots.positions: in the 4-panel: columns with 4 on top and bottom rows = vertical lines; rows with 4 at both ends = horizontal lines
slots.colours: k-th vertical line (left to right) gets legend's k-th vertical colour; k-th horizontal (top to bottom) gets legend's k-th horizontal colour
slots.crossings: per legend line: whichever colour is on top at that line's crossings in the legend stays on top

why: legend has as many vertical/horizontal lines as the marker panel marks; output lines sit exactly at marked rows/columns with legend colours and layering
invariants: output size equals the marker panel

reading: The input is two equal square halves: one is an 8 mask, the other a colour pattern. Output is their Kronecker product: each coloured cell becomes a copy of the mask painted in that colour, each background cell an empty block.

slots.mask: the half containing colour 8 (its 8 cells = shape)
slots.split: halves side by side or stacked, whichever gives two squares
slots.output: k*k by k*k grid, block (i,j) = mask recoloured with pattern[i][j], or empty if pattern[i][j] is 0

why: every k×k output block is the mask in the colour of the matching pattern cell, or all background
invariants: mask shape repeated unchanged in every non-empty block

reading: Left side holds 5x5 blocks, each either solid colour c or a 2-frame with a 3x3 pattern of 1s; the 8-panel legend shows one 3x3 pattern per colour. A solid c block becomes a 2-frame with legend-c's pattern in 1s; a patterned block becomes solid in the colour whose legend pattern matches it up to rotation/reflection.
verb: swap block between pattern and legend colour

slots.legend: on the 8-background panel: 3x3 shapes, one per colour
slots.solid_to_pattern: solid c block -> border 2, interior = legend-c shape as 1 (exact orientation), rest 2
slots.pattern_to_solid: 2-frame block with 1-pattern -> solid block of colour c whose legend shape equals the pattern under one of the 8 symmetries

why: each block's 3x3 interior pattern corresponds to exactly one legend colour (up to D4), and solid blocks map to their colour's exact legend shape

reading: Every pair of orthogonally adjacent red cells (a domino) gets a one-cell green (3) outline around it; isolated red cells are left alone.

new_rows.name: halo
new_rows.datalog:
orth(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 0.
orth(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DX = 0.
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
dom(O) :- osize(O, N), N = 2, obj(O, Y, X), orth(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, obj(O, Y2, X2).
halo(Y2, X2) :- dom(O), obj(O, Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, px(Y2, X2, C), !cell(Y2, X2, C).

why: the background cells 8-adjacent to a two-cell orthogonal red object are exactly the cells that become 3

reading: Each diagonal staircase band of 5s is coloured as nested L-shaped layers starting from its top end (corner at the top row's outer end, arms along the top row and down the outer column), layer k taking key colour k mod n from the key row; the leftover cap at the far end takes the last layer's colour.

slots.key: the short multi-coloured row segment (row 1), read left to right
slots.subject: each 8-connected 5-band (width w = length of its top row)
slots.layer: k = min(y - top_row, |x - outer_x_of_top_row|, rows - w), outer end = the side the band does not slant toward

why: every 5 cell gets key[k mod n] for its layer k; key row and background unchanged
